cases.why: THE DEFECT THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR (PR #15410, stranded ~11 hours). A genuine apt-budget install stall in build-and-test (ubuntu-24.04), the derived gate (required) roll-up, and a red `drift (loud)`. `drift (loud)` is deliberately NOT in the `gate (required)` needs: floor -- gate.yml says so in its own comment -- so its red blocks nothing and nothing about it can ever be resolved by a human either. The policy answered skip/mixed-failure and the run could only ever strand. With the floor derived from gate.yml it answers rerun, and the drift red is named in the detail rather than swallowed. Captured from GET /actions/runs/32886176743/attempts/1 because the run was manually re-run on 2026-08-26 before the fix existed.

note: REAL captured production data, not synthetic. Every run id, job id, step list and log excerpt
below was read from the GitHub Actions API of Lucent-Financial-Group/Zeta on 2026-08-25.
Log excerpts are LINE-NUMBERED slices of the real job log, keeping only lines a scanner could
key on (the apt banner lines, `##[error]Process completed with exit code N`, `command not
found`, and step-group headers). `logExcerpts[jobId].source` records the full log's byte and
line count so an excerpt can be checked against the original. The policy's checks are
substring/line tests, so an excerpt preserving the signature lines is a faithful stand-in and
one that drops them correctly fails to match.
Cases were chosen to include the NEGATIVES, because the negatives are the safety property:
one run mixing an install stall with genuine reds, and one run with only genuine reds.

APPENDED 2026-08-26: case 32886176743, captured from the runs/<id>/attempts/1 endpoint. It is the run whose skip/mixed-failure verdict is the defect that `non-blocking` closes; the other five cases are untouched, so every earlier assertion still measures what it measured.
